title: Query timeout option (SQL_ATTR_QUERY_TIMEOUT)
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
Previously the RODBCext package provided an option to set the [query timeout](https://github.com/zozlak/RODBCext/blob/master/R/odbcSetQueryTimeout.R). As of 2020 the package is deprecated and the better alternative is [odbc](https://github.com/r-dbi/odbc) ([cran](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/odbc/index.html)).

This odbc package doesn't seem to provide the described option. I was wondering if there is another way around to implement a query timeout while using odbc (perhaps something like the [C code](https://github.com/zozlak/RODBCext/blob/master/src/RODBCext.c#L426) of the RODBCext package which sets the value of SQL_ATTR_QUERY_TIMEOUT).

(R does have a [withTimeout](https://stackoverflow.com/q/70993017/1974344) function, but I want to have a reliable/ correct implementation)

The nanodbc.cpp file does have a [timeout function](https://github.com/r-dbi/odbc/blob/main/src/nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp#L1419) which sets the required SQL_ATTR_QUERY_TIMEOUT attribute, but this doesn't seem to be available in the R code?

### Database
Microsoft SQL Server

### Reproducible Example
con <- dbConnect(
  odbc::odbc(),
  driver = "SQL Server",
  server = "SERVERNAME",
  trusted_connection = TRUE,
  timeout = 5,
  encoding = "Latin1")

samplequery <- dbGetQuery(con, "
     SELECT * FROM [Something]   
")

title: Error when nvarchar(MAX) and/or varbinary(MAX) are in the SELECT statement while using bind parameters with multiple sets of values
description:
```R
library(DBI)
library(odbc)

mycon <- dbConnect(odbc::odbc(), Driver="ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server", Server = 'mydbserver', UID = 'myuid', PWD = 'mypasswd', database = 'mydb')

createTable <- dbExecute(mycon, "CREATE TABLE epi.dbo.People (id int NOT NULL, longid varbinary(MAX), name char(10) NOT NULL, comments nvarchar(MAX))")
insertRows <- dbExecute(mycon, "INSERT INTO epi.dbo.People (id, longid, name, comments) VALUES (1,1,'First','1st person'), (2,2,'Second','2nd person'), (3,3,'Third','3rd person')")

### Using dbGetQuery
### Works with one single set of values
mydf <- dbGetQuery(mycon,"select * from epi.dbo.People where id = ? and name = ?",params=list(2,'Second'))

### Does not work with two or more sets of values, i.e. batch of values
mydf <- dbGetQuery(mycon,"select * from epi.dbo.People where id = ? and name = ?",params=list(c(1,2),c('First','Second')))

### Two or more sets of values: works without nvarchar(MAX) or varbinary(MAX)
mydf <- dbGetQuery(mycon,"select id, name from epi.dbo.People where id = ? and name = ?",params=list(c(1,2),c('First','Second')))

### Two or more sets of values: does not work with nvarchar(MAX)
mydf <- dbGetQuery(mycon,"select id, name, comments from epi.dbo.People where id = ? and name = ?",params=list(c(1,2),c('First','Second')))

### Two or more sets of values: does not work with varbinary(MAX)
mydf <- dbGetQuery(mycon,"select id, name, longid from epi.dbo.People where id = ? and name = ?",params=list(c(1,2),c('First','Second')))


### Similar issue with dbSendQuery/dbBind/dbFetch 
myres <- dbSendQuery(mycon,"select * from epi.dbo.People where id = ? and name = ?")

### Single set of values works
dbBind(myres,params=list(c(2),c('Second')))
mydf <- dbFetch(myres)

### Two or more sets of values does not work
dbBind(myres,params=list(c(1,2),c('First','Second')))
mydf <- dbFetch(myres)
```

When it does not work, this is the error:
Error in result_fetch(res@ptr, n) : 
  nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:3280: HY109: [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server]Invalid cursor position

I think the error is caused by having a nvarchar(MAX) and/or varbinary(MAX) in the SELECT statement while using bind parameters with multiple sets of values.

When connecting to Microsoft SQL Server, the RStudio "Connections" tab shows "tables" and "views" but does not show "synonyms". ("Synonyms" also do not show-up when running `DBI::dbListTables(con)`)

If I want to view the synonyms in R I will typically do something like:

```
library(tidyverse)
```

title: add/update instructions for SQL Server test setup in `setup.md`
description:
The process to set up a Microsoft SQL Server is a bit different for M1, and we can also bump the versions on some of the installs.

Install Docker Desktop with:

```shell
brew install --cask docker
```

NOTE:
* You will need Docker 4.16 or higher
* You will need MacOS 13 Ventura (or higher)

For some reason I have trouble booting up `Docker.app` as usual, but the Docker Desktop app lives in `Docker.app > Show Package Contents > Contents > MacOS > Docker Desktop.app`.

For the driver and mssql install step,  bump to the most recent major driver version:

```shell
brew tap microsoft/mssql-release https://github.com/Microsoft/homebrew-mssql-release
brew install msodbcsql18 mssql-tools
```

In `odbc.ini`, I ended up with:

```ini
[MicrosoftSQLServer]
driver = SQL Server Driver
Server = 127.0.0.1
port = 1433
Encrypt = no
```

The `Encrypt = no` seems to be key. In  `odbcinst.ini`:

```ini
[SQL Server Driver]
Description=Microsoft ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server
Driver=/opt/homebrew/lib/libmsodbcsql.18.dylib
UsageCount=1
```

With dockers and the needed driver installed, I deployed the container with:

```shell
sudo docker run --platform linux/amd64 -e "ACCEPT_EULA=Y" -e "MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=BoopBop123!" \
   -p 1433:1433 --name sql1 --hostname sql1 \
   -d \
   mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest
```

The `--platform` tag is correct for M1; if you see `Status: Exited (1)` in Docker Desktop or a warning about incompatible architectures, navigate to `Settings > General` and ensure that `Use Rosetta for x86/amd64 emulation on Apple Silicon` is checked. I'm not sure why we'd use `server:2022-latest` rather than 2018, but I see errors with 2018.

To connect via odbc, we need to pass the UID and PWD via the connection string; I tried to configure via `odbc.ini`, but it seems that's [not permitted](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42387084/sql-server-odbc-driver-linux-username). U ise:

```r
mssql <- dbConnect(odbc::odbc(), dsn = "MicrosoftSQLServer", uid = "SA", pwd = "BoopBop123!")
```

title: note that drivers may not be automatically entered in `odbcinst.ini` on install
description: Much of the documentation I've found ([pyodbc docs](https://github.com/mkleehammer/pyodbc/wiki/Drivers-and-Driver-Managers#odbc-configuration-files-unix-only), [our docs](https://github.com/r-dbi/odbc/blob/777b8636aeab4018962bef88084f533c23e7549b/README.Rmd#L81-L98), for example) seems to suggest that `brew install`ing a driver will enter appropriate entries in the `odbcinst.ini` noted in `odbcinst -j` automatically. I've only seen this happen once after installing a few different drivers; it may be worth noting how to locate the install after `brew install`. I've been using `brew info` to get started.

title: note need to configure `odbcinst.ini` in `setup.md` demo
description:
In `setup.md`, the server test setup only describes how to configure the `odbc.ini` but not `odbcinst.ini`.

https://github.com/r-dbi/odbc/blob/777b8636aeab4018962bef88084f533c23e7549b/setup.md#L26-L34

This doc should outline how to locate the newly installed driver and refer to it in `odbcinst.ini`.

I was able to locate the driver by running `brew info msodbcsql17`, navigating to the folder referred to in the output (for me, `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/msodbcsql17/17.10.5.1`), and copying the entry from the `odbcinst.ini` in that folder.

In that `brew info` output, I also see:

```
==> Options
--without-registration
        Don't register the driver in odbcinst.ini
==> Caveats
If you installed this formula with the registration option (default), you'll
need to manually remove [ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server] section from
odbcinst.ini after the formula is uninstalled. This can be done by executing
the following command:
    odbcinst -u -d -n "ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server"
```

If installing with `without-registration` set appropriately will drop the entry in the same `.ini` file that this package will look to, we should just set that option.

title: Empty data.frame result from `dbGetQuery` if there is an `IF` statement in SQL Server query
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
`dbGetQuery()` returns an empty data.frame if there is an `IF` clause in the sql query.

### Database
SQL Server 2018

### Reproducible Example
Unfortunately, impossible to include the full query.

Essentially, there's a declared table `@Results` that has several select statements inserted into it.
For the final `insert into @Results select ....`, if add I add ```IF @some_var = 'thing'``` and then the exact same ```insert into select ...```,
```dbGetQuery()``` returns an empty data.frame with, 0 obs of 0 variables. Removing that `IF` from the sql query results in a proper filled data.frame with several columns.

I have `SET NOCOUNT ON` as mentioned [in this issue ](https://github.com/r-dbi/odbc/issues/173).

For a little better schematics of the whole query, here's the basic idea. The following works:
```
SET NOCOUNT ON
declare @Results table(...);
INSERT INTO @Results (...)
    SELECT ... from table1;

INSERT INTO @Results (...)
    SELECT ... from table2;

select * from @Results
```
This code returns a fully populated data.frame in R with `dbGetQuery()`.

However, if we add in an `IF` before that second `insert into` like

```
IF something
INSERT INTO @Results (...)
    SELECT ... from table2;
```

Then the resulting `data.frame` in R is 0 obs of 0 columns.

title: Snowflake INSERTs are very slow
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
RStudio ODBC driver does not effectively take advantage of parallelization in Snowflake as compared with SQL Server. INSERT functions in Snowflake are executed sequentially, which results in slower performance. 

### Database
Snowflake 6.22.0

### Reproducible Example


**ODBC Connections**
```
library(tidyverse)
library(odbc)
library(DBI)
library(glue)
library(rbenchmark)
library(parallel)

sqlCon <- dbConnect(odbc(), dsn='XXXXX', timeout=60*60, database='XXXXX')

snowCon <- dbConnect(odbc(), dsn='snowflake', warehouse='XXXXX_WH',
                     PRIV_KEY_FILE_PWD=rstudioapi::askForPassword("Passphrase for key: "),
                     role="XXXXX",
                     database="XXXXX",
                     schema="DBO"

numCores <- 8
repeatQuery <- 10
```
**Test 1: Select performance (SELECT TOP 10 MM)**
```
qry <- 'SELECT TOP 10000000 *
        FROM "XXXXX_db"."DBO"."V_XXXXX"
        '

read_perf <- benchmark(
  Read_SQLServer = {
    dbGetQuery(sqlCon, qry)
  },
  Read_Snowflake = {
    dbGetQuery(snowCon, qry)
  },
  replications = repeatQuery
)

knitr::kable(read_perf)
```
> |   |test           | replications| elapsed| relative| user.self| sys.self| user.child| sys.child|
> |:--|:--------------|------------:|-------:|--------:|---------:|--------:|----------:|---------:|
> |2  |Read_Snowflake |           10| 211.047|    1.268|   205.212|   16.197|          0|         0|
> |1  |Read_SQLServer |           10| 166.406|    1.000|   149.501|   16.452|          0|         0|

**Test 2: Write performance (100 columns, 100K rows)**
```
source("customWrite.R")

big_table <- as.data.frame(round(MASS::mvrnorm(n=1e5, mu=1:100, Sigma=diag(1:100)),3))

write_perf <- benchmark(
  Write_SQLServer = {
    customWriteTable(sqlCon, targetChar = "t_big_table", sourceDf = big_table, overwrite = TRUE)
  },
  Write_Snowflake = {
    customWriteTable(snowCon, targetChar = "t_big_table", sourceDf = big_table, overwrite = TRUE)
  },
  replications = repeatQuery
)

knitr::kable(write_perf)
```

> |   |test            | replications| elapsed| relative| user.self| sys.self| user.child| sys.child|
> |:--|:---------------|------------:|-------:|--------:|---------:|--------:|----------:|---------:|
> |2  |Write_Snowflake |           10| 356.456|    8.875|   203.692|    3.786|      0.205|     0.182|
> |1  |Write_SQLServer |           10|  40.165|    1.000|    14.619|    2.335|      0.000|     0.000|

**Test 3: Concurrent writes**
_100 columns, 360 rows, 8 concurrent writes, 100 repeats_
```
set.seed(123)

rowIndex <- vector("list", 100)
rowIndex <- lapply(rowIndex, function(x) sample(1:nrow(big_table), 360))

subset_and_write <- function(index, con){
  if(con@info$dbms.name == 'Microsoft SQL Server') {
    con <- dbConnect(odbc(), dsn='BI_17', timeout=60*60)
  }
  
  customWriteTable(con, targetChar = "t_big_table", sourceDf = big_table[index,], append = TRUE)
}

write_concur_perf <- benchmark(
  Write_Concur_SQLServer = {
    mclapply(rowIndex, subset_and_write, con=sqlCon, mc.cores=numCores)
  },
  Write_Concur_Snowflake = {
    mclapply(rowIndex, subset_and_write, con=snowCon, mc.cores=numCores)
  },
  replications = repeatQuery
)

knitr::kable(write_concur_perf)
```
> |   |test                   | replications| elapsed| relative| user.self| sys.self| user.child| sys.child|
> |:--|:----------------------|------------:|-------:|--------:|---------:|--------:|----------:|---------:|
> |2  |Write_Concur_Snowflake |           10| 278.674|   19.297|     1.687|    9.049|    112.092|    22.192|
> |1  |Write_Concur_SQLServer |           10|  14.441|    1.000|     0.116|    4.901|     14.682|    11.200|

**Custom Write Table Source File**
```
customWriteTable <- function(conn, targetChar, sourceDf, overwrite=FALSE, append=FALSE, batch_size=50000, ...){
  
  original_settings <- getOption("odbc.batch_rows", 1024)
  
  options(odbc.batch_rows=batch_size)
  
  if(overwrite==TRUE & append==TRUE){
    stop("Only one arg can be TRUE: overwrite and append.")
  }
  
  if(overwrite==TRUE){
    qry <- glue_sql("drop table if exists ", targetChar, .con=conn)
    dbExecute(conn, qry)
    dbWriteTable(conn, targetChar, value=sourceDf, batch_rows = batch_size, ...)
    
  } else if(append==TRUE){
    if(conn@info$dbms.name == 'Microsoft SQL Server') {
      dbWriteTable(conn, value=sourceDf, name = targetChar, overwrite = FALSE, append = TRUE,
                   row.names=FALSE, batch_rows = batch_size)
    } else(
      #  **dbWriteTable() fails in Snowflake for appends**
      dbAppendTable(conn, targetChar, value=sourceDf, batch_rows = batch_size, ...) 
    )
  } else{
    dbWriteTable(conn, targetChar, value=sourceDf, batch_rows = batch_size, ...)
  }
  options(odbc.batch_rows=original_settings)
}
```

title: Support for automatic credential refresh with supported drivers
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result

Right now if you're using an OAuth2 token instead of a username/password with certain drivers and the token expires, queries start returning errors.

Microsoft has a section on this [in the ODBC 4.0 spec](https://github.com/microsoft/ODBC-Specification/blob/master/ODBC%204.0.md#324-token-expiration), and there's more precise detail in the documentation for the Databricks driver itself:

![manual1](https://github.com/r-dbi/odbc/assets/1448326/60244916-3a38-4353-8fe6-bd9a5a28c327)
![manual2](https://github.com/r-dbi/odbc/assets/1448326/c5688e09-0b87-4e1f-82a9-be72b9a6ebd5)

I'm wondering if it's possible to catch these errors, refresh the tokens (if possible), and retry the query automatically.

### Database

Databricks, but potentially others.

### Reproducible Example

I'm not sure I can provide a reproducible example for this, it's transient and requires all of the OAuth2 stuff to be set up.

<details>
<summary>Session Info</summary>

```r
devtools::session_info()
#> output
```
</details>

title: Password authentication error with Amazon Redshift if certain characters are present in the password
description:
```
library(odbc)
  con <- dbConnect(odbc::odbc(), 
  driver = "Redshift", 
  server = abc.redhsift.amazonaws.com, 
  database = db_name, 
  uid = abc,
  pwd = password,
  port = 1234)
```  
returns
**Error: nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:1135: 0000: [RStudio][AmazonRedshift] (10) Error occured while trying to connect: [SQLState 28000] connection to server "abc.redhsift.amazonaws.com" , port 1234 failed: FATAL: password authentication failed for user "abc".**

I do not see this error when I try connecting to Redshift using Python. My observation is that the whenever the Redshift password contains the characters **[]{}(),;?*=!@** it fails with the above error. The Redshift documentation [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/configure-odbc-connection.html#:~:text=following%20special%20characters%3A-,%5B%5D%7B%7D()%2C%3B%3F*%3D!%40,-If%20you%20use) suggests to wrap the password inside curly braces **{}** whenever these characters are present but wrapping them inside curly braces does not work with odbc.

### Database
Amazon Redshift

title: Name and schema in DBI::Id
description:
*@troelsy commented on Aug 9, 2018, 8:03 AM UTC:*

I think I found a bug when working with DBI::Id. DBI::Id requires that you specify 'name' and 'schema', which makes sense, but the order of the arguments must be schema-name and not name-schema. It seems like it doesn't actually use the name of the arguments.

I made this example, to show the error. You can try with both 'table_id'

```
library(odbc)
library(DBI)

con <- dbConnect(odbc(),
                   Driver = "PostgreSQL Unicode",
                   Server = "...",
                   Database = "...",
                   UID = "...",
                   PWD = "...",
                   Port = 5432)

data <- data.frame("x" = c(1, 2), "y" = c(2,1))
print(data)

# table_id <- DBI::Id(name = "my_table", schema = "my_schema")
table_id <- DBI::Id(schema="my_schema", name = "my_table")
print(table_id)

DBI::dbWriteTable(con, table_id, data, overwrite = TRUE)

```

If you run it as is, you'll get:

```
$ Rscript test.R
Loading required package: methods
  x y
1 1 2
2 2 1
<Id> name = my_schema, schema = my_table

```

If you use the other definition of 'table_id', you'll get:

```
$ Rscript test.R
Loading required package: methods
  x y
1 1 2
2 2 1
<Id> name = my_table, schema = my_schema
Error: <SQL> 'CREATE TABLE "my_table"."my_schema" (
  "x" DOUBLE PRECISION,
  "y" DOUBLE PRECISION
)
'
  nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:1587: 3F000: ERROR: schema "my_table" does not exist;
Error while executing the query
Execution halted

```

Notice the error message saying the schema is "my_table". I'm using Ubuntu 16.04.4 LTS with PostgreSQL 9.5.12

*This issue was moved by [krlmlr](https://github.com/krlmlr) from [r-dbi/DBI#255](https://github.com/r-dbi/DBI/issues/255).*

```
ld: in cctz/libcctz.a, archive has no table of contents
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
make: *** [odbc.so] Error 1
```
To ensure the build works, either set correct flags explicitly or run `ranlib`.

title: RStudio IDE Connection Pane issue when connecting to Databricks SQL Warehouse
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result

When connecting to a Databricks SQL Warehouse, this is how the RStudio IDE's Connection pane should look. The user is able to expand "catalogs", to see "schemas" (they call it Databases), and then expand to see tables. The following screenshot is how it looks when using [`sparklyr` to connect:](https://spark.rstudio.com/deployment/databricks-spark-connect.html) 

![image](https://github.com/r-dbi/odbc/assets/77294576/1ae2d618-e726-4df6-beaf-aba9684fd21f)

The next screenshot, shows how the Connections pane looks when using `odbc` in the following code:

```r
con <- dbConnect(
  odbc::odbc(),
  Driver = "/Library/simba/spark/lib/libsparkodbc_sb64-universal.dylib",
  Host = "[Databricks URL for the Organizations host]",
  Port = 443,
  AuthMech = 3,
  HTTPPath = "/sql/1.0/warehouses/300bd24ba12adf8e",
  Protocol = "https",
  ThriftTransport = 2,
  SSL = 1,
  UID = "token",
  PWD = Sys.getenv("DATABRICKS_TOKEN")
  )
```
![image](https://github.com/r-dbi/odbc/assets/77294576/37a48d05-380b-4fd4-bc93-a510580f6dfd)

When we specify the `catalog` to use, the Connections pane improves. It shows the schema and tables, but, as seen in the following screenshot, it shows the exact same schema and tables beneath all of the catalogs, instead of only the one that we selected.

```r
con <- dbConnect(
  odbc::odbc(),
  Driver = "/Library/simba/spark/lib/libsparkodbc_sb64-universal.dylib",
  Host = "[Databricks URL for the Organizations host]",

  AuthMech = 3,

  ThriftTransport = 2,
  SSL = 1,
  UID = "token",
```

![image](https://github.com/r-dbi/odbc/assets/77294576/84e74b8f-cd62-487f-a20b-9fb32992e8d1)


### Database
[Databricks SQL Warehouse](https://docs.databricks.com/en/sql/index.html) via their [ODBC driver](https://docs.databricks.com/en/sql/index.html)

Because this is related to the Connection pane, there is no real reprex to provide, the connection code provided above should lead to the same results.

title: Character columns in SQL Server with R 3.6
description:

Since updating to R 3.6.0, columns of type **character** come through to R garbled.

I updated to R 3.6.0 last night and discovered that columns that are text/character no longer are brought into memory in R correctly. This looks like the same thing reported in #279 with dropping even-indexed characters.

title: MSSQL: Cannot append to temporary tables
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
Unable to append to temporary table due to `dbExistsTable` being blind to temporary tables. Given that the table exists and can be queried from, I expect to be able to append to it.

May be related to #509 ?

### Database
Microsoft SQL Server 16.0.1000.6

### Reproducible Example

```r
library(odbc)
library(DBI)

con <- DBI::dbConnect(odbc::odbc(),
                                Driver = "ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server",
                                SERVER = "<masked>",
                                Trusted_Connection="yes",
                                TrustServerCertificate="yes",
                                port = 1433)

dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE #my_temp (
               id int not null,
               x float not null,
               primary key (id)
               )", immediate=TRUE) # need immediate=TRUE for table to continue to exist
#> [1] 0

# We can verify that the table exists through select
dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM #my_temp")
#> [1] id x 
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

dbAppendTable(con, "#my_temp", data.frame(id=1, x=5.0))
#> Error in dbAppendTable(con, "#my_temp", data.frame(id = 1, x = 5)): dbExistsTable(conn, name) is not TRUE
dbExistsTable(con, "#my_temp")
#> [1] FALSE
dbExistsTable(con, "#my_temp", immediate=TRUE)
#> [1] FALSE
```
It may be worth mentioning that I also experience this same issue on a Linux system as well.

title: Issues connecting to Oracle database where ROracle succeeds (`ORA-12504`, `"Data source name not found, and no default driver specified "`)
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result I am trying to connect to an Oracle database via ODBC, but I'm not having any luck so far. I have used `RJDBC` in the past and after some headaches I managed to get `ROracle` running, but ODBC is giving me some trouble as I find e.g. inconsistent information online and am unfortunately not sure how to debug this as I can't simply `debugonce(debConnect)`. For background, I have read among other resources: - https://solutions.posit.co/connections/db/databases/oracle/#connection-settings and related docs - https://r-dbi.github.io/odbc/index.html#connecting-to-a-database - https://www.connectionstrings.com/oracle/ - https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/21/lnoci/build-and-configure-oci-applications.html#GUID-E97921AA-A166-44EB-97B7-9EEFE3A23ED3 and related docs My successful connection via `ROracle` looks like this, with IP, DB etc changed: ```r library(ROracle) library(DBI) con <- dbConnect( ROracle::Oracle(), username = "", password = "", dbname = "12.345.67.89:1521/OurCoolDatabase" ) con ``` ``` User name: Connect string: 12.345.67.89:1521/OurCoolDatabase Server version: 11.2.0.2.0 Server type: Oracle RDBMS Results processed: 5 OCI prefetch: FALSE ``` Translating to ODBC would be simple I thought, but I guess the fact that the `dbConnect()` arguments are different was the first hint that it's going to be harder than I hoped: ```r library(odbc) con <- DBI::dbConnect( odbc::odbc(), Driver = "Oracle21", Host = "12.345.67.89", SVC = "OurCoolDatabase", # I tried different things here to no avail. UID = "", PWD = "", Port = 1521 ) ``` This yields this error: ``` Error: nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:1135: 00000: [Oracle][ODBC][Ora]ORA-12504: TNS:listener was not given the SERVICE_NAME in CONNECT_DATA ``` After some googling around I found that adding `dsn = "12.345.67.89:1521/OurCoolDatabase"` could work, which at least changed the error I guess: ``` Error: nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:1135: 00000: [unixODBC][Driver Manager]Data source name not found, and no default driver specified ``` I also tried connecting via a dedicated connection, so variations of this: ```r con <- DBI::dbConnect(odbc::odbc(), "cooldb", pwd = "") con <- dbConnect( odbc::odbc(), "cooldb", UID = "", PWD = "", .connection_string = "DBQ=12.345.67.89:1521/OurCoolDatabase" ) ``` but did not receive any more useful results. I am reasonably certain I have set up `odbcinst.ini` correctly, but not so much for `~/.odbc.ini`. In any case, I would like to note that both of these find the entries I expect: ```r odbc::odbcListDrivers() odbc::odbcListDataSources() ```
Contents of /etc/odbcinst.ini: ```ini [Oracle21] Description = Oracle ODBC driver for Oracle 21.1 Driver = /usr/lib/oracle/21/client64/lib/libsqora.so.21.1 Setup = FileUsage = CPTimeout = CPReuse = ``` I have installed the ODBC driver from Oracle and have verified that `/usr/lib/oracle/21/client64/lib/libsqora.so.21.1` exists. `unixodb{-dev}` are also installed.
Contents of ~/.odbc.ini (schematically): ```ini [cooldb] Description = "Our Cool Database" Driver = Oracle21 Database = OurCoolDatabase Servername = 12.345.67.89 UserName = Port = 1521 ``` I'd like to note that I have not fully understood what the correct names for these entries should be, as everything that comes up via google appears to use slightly different names

title: [Teradata] `dbListTables` broken by odbc 1.3.5
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result

In Teradata method for dbListTables, the argument `table_name` is not renamed into the argument `name` expected by the new function `odbcConnectionTables`.  It was caused by #577.
See code in https://github.com/r-dbi/odbc/blob/main/R/db.R#L108C1-L113C5

### Database

Teradata 17.20

### Reproducible Example

```r
con <- DBI::dbConnect(odbc::odbc(), dsn = "my_teradata_dsn")

DBI::dbListTables(con, table_name = "my_table")
```

The code works with odbc 1.3.4 and fails with odbc 1.3.5
```
Error in .local(conn, name, ...) : 
  argument not used (table_name = "my_table")
```

title: very long text is truncated upon UPDATE
description:
Coming over from https://github.com/tidyverse/dbplyr/issues/1327:


I am working with a remote MySQL database trough dplyr / dbplyr and inserting a very long text (JSON) into a column with Type LONGTEXT (which has enough space to store the string in the db)

I experienced truncation of the string to maximum 65535 characters (byte limit for e.g. TEXT columns) when using `dplyr::rows_update` . When using an alternative approach using DBI directly this truncation does not occur. 

apparently the process id not detect / respect the length of the data at hand and inserted truncated data without issuing a warning.

I was asked to open an issue for RMariaDB, which I am doing now.

Reprex:
```
library(DBI)
library(dplyr)

con <- dbConnect(RMariaDB::MariaDB(),
                 host = "your_server", dbname="your_db", timeout=10,
                 user = Sys.getenv("MYSQL_USER"), password = Sys.getenv("MYSQL_PW")
)

# Create a sample data frame with long JSON data
json_data <- paste(rep('{"key":"', 100000), "a", rep('"}', 100000), collapse = "")
json_data <- paste0('{"data": "', json_data, '"}')

df <- data.frame(id = 1:3, json = rep(json_data, 3))

print(nchar(json_data))

# Create Table in remote database with name `temp_table` with a column `json` set to LONGTEXT
# Create the table
query <- "
  CREATE TABLE temp_table (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    json LONGTEXT
  )
"
dbExecute(con, query)

# Use dplyr to update the remote database table

tbl(con, "temp_table") %>%
  rows_insert(df,by = c("id"), copy=TRUE, in_place = TRUE, conflict="ignore")

resDplyr <- tbl(con,"temp_table") %>%
  dplyr::collect()

nchar(resDplyr$json[1])


# DBI method -----------------------------------------------------------------
update_statement <- "UPDATE temp_table SET json = ? WHERE id = ? "


# Iterate over the rows in the data frame and update the database
for (i in seq_len(nrow(df))) {
  # Get the values for the current row
  json_data <- df$json[i]
  id <- df$id[i]
  
  # Execute the update statement with the current row values
  dbExecute(con, update_statement, list(json_data, id))
}

resDBI <- tbl(con,"temp_table") %>%
  dplyr::collect()

nchar(resDBI$json[1])

# Close the database connection
dbDisconnect(con)
```

title: Invalid SQL data type error when viewing table columns in RStudio Connections pane
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
I'm using odbc on a Windows 10 machine to connect R to our Oracle datawarehouse.

I can connect and use dplyr in the console just fine. However, if I use the RStudio Connections pane, I'm able to see all the schemas and tables, but when I try to expand a table to see the columns in that table, I get an error.

First, RStudio pops up a dialog box saying "R code execution error"

Then, in the console, I see more details about the error, namely:

```
Error in connection_sql_columns(connection@ptr, table_name = validateObjectName(table,  :
```

My connection string looks like this:

title: Login timeout expired connecting to serverless Azure SQL Database when paused
description:
Not sure if this is an error in `odbc` or in Azure SQL Database, but if you are using [serverless mode](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sql-database/sql-database-serverless) and the database has auto-paused, creating the connection fails:

```R
> constr="
Driver={SQL Server};Server=tcp:REDACTED.database.windows.net,1433;Database=retail;Uid=REDACTED@REDACTED;Pwd=REDACTED;Encrypt=yes;TrustServerCertificate=no;Connection Timeout=30;
"
> con <- dbConnect(odbc(), .connection_string=constr)
Error: nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:950: HYT00: [Microsoft][ODBC SQL Server Driver]Login timeout expired 
```

The workaround is to wait 10-20 seconds for the database to warm up, and run the `dbConnect` call again.

More info in this blog post: https://blog.revolutionanalytics.com/2019/08/azure-sql-serverless.html . If you think this is an error in how Azure SQL Database responds to the connection request, let me know and I will pass that along to the Azure team.

title: S4 method cleanup
description:
Consolidate calls to:

* connection_sql_columns, and
* connection_sql_tables

in S4 methods.  The former already has a an S4 method, however we still call it directly outside the S4 method.  The latter needs an S4 method, and all internal callers ( there are several ) need to be transitioned to call the S4 method.

That way, if a particular DBMS needs an adjusted `connection_sql_tables` call, for example, we can specialize the S4 method and all callers will benefit.

```
$ grep -r --include=\*.R --exclude=RcppExports.R 'connection_sql_tables'
```

title: Signature differences for sqlCreateTable compared to DBI function specification
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
<!--Example: `dbGetQuery()` returns incorrect timestamps.-->
Incorrect function signature for `sqlCreateTable` in `R/db.R` The following snippet is the signature given by odbc package:
```
setMethod("sqlCreateTable", "Teradata",
  function(con, table, fields, field.types = NULL, row.names = NA, temporary = FALSE, ...) {
    table <- dbQuoteIdentifier(con, table)
    fields <- createFields(con, fields, field.types, row.names)

    SQL(paste0(
        "CREATE ", if (temporary) " MULTISET VOLATILE ", "TABLE ", table, " (\n",
        "  ", paste(fields, collapse = ",\n  "), "\n)\n", if (temporary) " ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS"
        ))
  })
```
However, the signature in DBI specification is **(note that field.types argument is not present)**:

![sql_create_table](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/24271764/112048874-de7af780-8b74-11eb-889e-e1e648501627.PNG)

### Database
Teradata

### Reproducible Example
```r
library(odbc)
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(odbc::odbc(), dsn = "TeradataDSN")
# row_names column is not created even though "row.names" argument is set to TRUE.
> query <- sqlCreateTable(con, table = "rock_table", fields = rock, row.names = TRUE)
> query
<SQL> CREATE TABLE "rock_table" (
  "area" INTEGER,
  "peri" FLOAT,
  "shape" FLOAT,
  "perm" FLOAT
)
# Note that temporary table is not created and row_names column is created, even though the  "temporary"
# argument is set and "row.names" argument is NA.
> query <- sqlCreateTable(con, table = "rock_table", fields = rock, row.names = NA, temporary = TRUE)
> query
<SQL> CREATE TABLE "rock_table" (
  "row_names" VARCHAR(255),
  "area" INTEGER,
  "peri" FLOAT,
  "shape" FLOAT,
  "perm" FLOAT
)
# Note that temporary table is created when there is additional TRUE (which is part of ... in function definition)
> query <- sqlCreateTable(con, table = "rock_table", fields = rock, row.names = NA, temporary = TRUE, TRUE)
> query
<SQL> CREATE  MULTISET VOLATILE TABLE "rock_table" (
  "row_names" VARCHAR(255),
  "area" INTEGER,
  "peri" FLOAT,
  "shape" FLOAT,
  "perm" FLOAT
)
 ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS
# getMethod call
> getMethod("sqlCreateTable", "Teradata")
Method Definition:

function (con, table, fields, row.names = NA, temporary = FALSE, 
    ...) 
{
    .local <- function (con, table, fields, field.types = NULL, 
        row.names = NA, temporary = FALSE, ...) 
    {
        table <- dbQuoteIdentifier(con, table)
        fields <- createFields(con, fields, field.types, row.names)
        SQL(paste0("CREATE ", if (temporary) 
            " MULTISET VOLATILE ", "TABLE ", table, 
            " (\n", "  ", paste(fields, collapse = ",\n  "), 
            "\n)\n", if (temporary) 
                " ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS"))
    }
    .local(con, table, fields, row.names, temporary, ...)
}
<bytecode: 0x000001f6f015a660>
<environment: namespace:odbc>

Signatures:
        con       
target  "Teradata"
defined "Teradata"
```

## Possible issue
Note that from **`getMethod`** call that the function passes the arguments to `.local()` function, which does not use named arguments but just positional argument and there is `field.types` argument in `.local()` which is not part of `sqlCreateTable`. Hence, `row.names` is passed to `field.types`, `temporary` is passed to `row.names` and TRUE (as part of ...) is passed to `temporary`.
**The behavior is same when column types is provided in the argument `fields` as per DBI sqlCreateTable specification.**
```r
# Note that temporary table is not created and row_names column is created, even though the  "temporary"
# argument is set and "row.names" argument is NA.
> query <- sqlCreateTable(con, table = "rock_table", fields = rock_types, row.names = NA, temporary = TRUE)
> query
<SQL> CREATE TABLE "rock_table" (
  "area" integer,
  "peri" float,
  "shape" decimal(5, 2),
  "perm" decimal(15, 3)
)
# Note that temporary table is created when there is additional TRUE (which is part of ... in function definition)
> query <- sqlCreateTable(con, table = "rock_table", fields = rock_types, row.names = NA, temporary = TRUE, TRUE)
> query
<SQL> CREATE  MULTISET VOLATILE TABLE "rock_table" (
  "area" integer,
  "peri" float,
  "shape" decimal(5, 2),
  "perm" decimal(15, 3)
)
 ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS
```

title: fatal errors in Windows with odbc 1.2.3
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
After updating to odbc 1.2.3, RStudio gives a fatal error (a popup window which requires a restart of RStudio) in cases where I used to get an informative 'nanodbc' error (text in the console itself) in previous versions of odbc.  Reinstalling odbc 1.2.2 solves the problem.

When debugging the fatal error, I get the following message:

![VSerror (1)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18716476/90616704-0cc6dc00-e20e-11ea-8ece-45b4dd8b0a25.png)

As I don't have Visual Studio installed on my computer, I cannot follow [this advice](https://docs.microsoft.com/nl-be/visualstudio/debugger/just-in-time-debugging-in-visual-studio?view=vs-2015&redirectedfrom=MSDN) to solve the problem.  I don't understand completely, does the new code in odbc 1.2.3 somehow triggers to use this program?  Or does it just throw an error message that RStudio on Windows cannot handle?

In any case, it is impossible for me (and probably other Windows users) to update to odbc 1.2.3 as long as this problem persists.  I hope it can be solved in future versions of odbc?

### Database
SQL Server 2016 (on Windows 7 OS)

### Reproducible Example
Example:
```r
library(odbc)
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(odbc(), driver = "SQL Server", server = "our_institure_server", port = 1433,
                 database = "test", trusted_connection = TRUE, encoding = "latin1")
# If the database server is not accessible, a fatal error would occur here
# (odbc 1.2.2 would give: Error: nanodbc/nanodbd.cpp:983: 01s00: [Microsoft][ODBC SQL Server driver]...
#       'SQL server does not exist or access to server is denied.')
dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM X")
# if table `X` contains a column with format varchar(max) that is not the last column, a fatal error occurs
# (odbc 1.2.2 would give the 'invalid descriptor index' error discussed in issue #309)
```

title: Why is ‘include <codecvt>’ required for odbc 1.2.3 or 1.3.0?
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result

Could you release versions of `odbc` not dependent on `<codecvt>`?

I haven’t been able to use our RStudio Pro Servers for months for work with an Azure MS SQL database because odbc 1.2.3 (and now odbc 1.3.0) will not compile on our servers -- and odbc 1.2.2 had no problems compiling but has execution problems.

The new versions of `odbc` won’t compile because of a new requirement for `include <codecvt>`:

### Reproducible Example

```
devtools::install_version("odbc", version = "1.2.3", repos = "https://cran.rstudio.com/")
```

and

```
devtools::install_version("odbc", version = "1.3.0", repos = "https://cran.rstudio.com/")
```

have exactly the same compilation issue that was not present compiling odbc 1.2.2.:

```
nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:40:19: fatal error: codecvt: No such file or directory
 #include <codecvt>
                   ^
compilation terminated.
make: *** [nanodbc.o] Error 1
ERROR: compilation failed for package ‘odbc’
```

We’re using CentOS 7, which supposedly has an end-of-life on July 7, 2024.  https://endoflife.software/operating-systems/linux/centos

Admittedly, our gcc compiler is a bit old but does compile odbc 1.2.2 successfully:

```
gcc –version
gcc (GCC) 4.8.5 20150623 (Red Hat 4.8.5-16)
```

Our admins tell me:  “Upgrading gcc will impact the compilation of all software on the server and so I do not know if we want to upgrade at this time.  ”

Why can’t RStudio support CentOS 7 for its full lifetime?

### Details

Newer odbc versions fixed bugs and added new features that I cannot now use on our RStudio Pro Server yet.   

Why must I use my PC and local RStudio Workstation to access a database that does not work from our RStudio Servers? 

This simple example works fine on a PC with newer versions of odbc, either 1.2.3 or 1.3.0, but not on our servers with odbc 1.2.2:

```{r}
HealthFacts <- 
  dbConnect(odbc(),
            Driver   = "ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server",
            Server   = SERVER,
            Database = DATABASE,
            UID      = Sys.getenv("HF_UID"),  # from .Renviron file
            PWD      = Sys.getenv("HF_PWD"),
            Encrypt  = ifelse(Sys.info()["sysname"] == "Linux",
                             "yes",
                             "no"),
            TrustServerCertificate = "no",
            Connection_Timeout     = 30,
            bigint   = "integer")
```

```{r}
# Create small temporary table

tempName <- paste0("efg_temp_", format(Sys.time(), "%Y%m%d_%H%M%S"))
tempData <- tibble(a = c("A", "B", "C"),
                   i = 1:3)
tempTable <- copy_to(HealthFacts, tempData, tempName, temporary = TRUE)
```

title: `dbWriteTable()` fails on either append or overwrite for Teradata
description:
*@neiljohnramal-teradata commented on Sep 28, 2018, 5:02 AM UTC:*

`DBI::dbReadTable` can read tables in Teradata regardless of letter-casing but `dbWriteTable` would fail unless the table name matches completely (case and all).

```r
library(DBI)
library(odbc)

con <- dbConnect(
  odbc(),
  Driver = "/path/to/teradata/driver",
  DBCName = "address",
  UID = "user",
  PWD = "password"
)

# table name is some_table

w <- dbReadTable(con, Id(schema = "some_schema", table = "some_table")) # works
x <- dbReadTable(con, Id(schema = "some_schema", table = "SOME_TABLE")) # also works

vals <- read.csv("items.csv")
y <- dbWriteTable(
  con, Id(schema = "some_schema", table = "some_table"), vals, overwrite = TRUE
) # works
z <- dbWriteTable(
  con, Id(schema = "some_schema", table = "SOME_TABLE"), vals, overwite = TRUE
) # Error: 'SOME_TABLE' already exists
```

It does not produce an error that the table does not exist but instead it would say that the table already exists.

*This issue was moved by [krlmlr](https://github.com/krlmlr) from [r-dbi/DBI#262](https://github.com/r-dbi/DBI/issues/262).*

title: dbAppendTable not adding data to Hive table inside a schema
description:
*@bjoerm commented on Jul 3, 2018, 10:53 AM UTC:*

Hey guys,
Thanks a lot for all the work on connecting R with various databases!

I encountered problems when I tried to write data via DBI::dbAppendTable into a Hive database (that uses schemas).

I am using R 3.5, DBI 1.0.0, odbc 1.1.6 within RStudio 1.1.453 on a Windows 10 computer.

### Summary:

*   Connecting to the database via odbc works fine.
*   Executing dbGetQuery to SELECT, DROP, CREATE stuff works fine.
*   dbCreateTable, dbRemoveTable, dbExistsTable and dbReadTable work fine when used in combination with DBI::Id.
*   dbAppendTable however only returns a "0" in the R console (no error message) and does not add any values to tables.

### Details/Code (from our Hive database, so not easily reproduceabe):

Please find below the reduced code. Comments inside the code show the errors the were returned.

```r
# Packages ----------------------------------------------------------------

library(odbc)
library(DBI)
library(tibble)

# Connecting via odbc -----------------------------------------------------

con <- DBI::dbConnect(
  drv = odbc::odbc()
  , dsn = "hive" # Cloudera ODBC Driver for Apache Hive (64-bit)
)

# Setting up the path to the table
table_name <- DBI::Id(schema = "workspace_analytics", table = "bm_r_test")

# Trying to append data ---------------------------------------------------

# Following the example from https://www.r-dbi.org/blog/dbi-2-final/

DBI::dbCreateTable(con, table_name, c(a = "char")) # Works
DBI::dbAppendTable(con, table_name, data.frame(a = "tree"))
# Returns to console: [1] 0 and does not write values into the table.

DBI::dbReadTable(con, table_name) %>% tibble::as.tibble()
# Returns an empty tibble:
## A tibble: 0 x 1
## ... with 1 variable: a <chr>

DBI::dbRemoveTable(con, table_name)
DBI::dbCreateTable(con, table_name, c(a = "int", b = "float"))
DBI::dbAppendTable(con, table_name, data.frame(a = 1:3, b = 1:3))

DBI::dbReadTable(con, table_name) %>% tibble::as.tibble()
# Returns an empty tibble as well:
## A tibble: 0 x 2
## ... with 2 variables: a <int>, b <dbl>

# Approach via dbWriteTable
DBI::dbRemoveTable(con, table_name)

DBI::dbWriteTable(con, table_name, value = data.frame(a = 1:3, b = 1:3))
# Error: Can't unquote `workspace_analytics`.`bm_r_test`

DBI::dbCreateTable(con, table_name, c(a = "char")) # Works
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, table_name, data.frame(a = "tree"), append = TRUE)
# Error: Can't unquote `workspace_analytics`.`bm_r_test`

DBI::dbReadTable(con, table_name_mtcars) # Thus, returns a table with correct columns but with zero rows.
```

tl;dr: dbAppendTable does not append data into our Hive database. Instead of showing an error, it just returns a "0" to the console.

Can you help me out? Do you need any additional information? Do you have a lead on what I might try (e.g. how to get a closer look on what dbAppendTable is doing here and why it is not returning any error).

Again, thanks a lot for your work!

*This issue was moved by [krlmlr](https://github.com/krlmlr) from [r-dbi/DBI#250](https://github.com/r-dbi/DBI/issues/250).*

title: Encoding of Azure Data Warehouse secret key leads to base-64 error
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
Using dbExecute to run a query that contains a storage account key fails with _Error: nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:1617: 42000: [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server][SQL Server]The input is not a valid Base-64 string as it contains a non-base 64 character, more than two padding characters, or an illegal character among the padding characters._

Running the same thing using RODBC's sqlQuery is successful. Running the same SQL query in SQL Server Management Studio also works.

My guess is it has to do with the way the characters in the storage account key are encoded before being send to the data warehouse, especially the / and + characters, but I am not sure. If that is the issue, I am also not sure how to change how the key is encoded.

### Database
Azure Data Warehouse/Synapse Analytics

### Reproducible Example
Difficult to give a reproducible example because of the specifics but here is the code I'm running:

```r
library(odbc)
library(DBI)
library(keyring)

con <- DBI::dbConnect(odbc::odbc(),
                       driver = "ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server",
                       server = "tcp:<server>database.windows.net,1433",
                       database = "<db_name>",
                       uid = keyring::key_list("<db_name>")[["username"]],
                       pwd = keyring::key_get("<db_name>", keyring::key_list("<db_name>")[["username"]]),
                       Encrypt = "yes",
                       TrustServerCertificate = "yes",
                       Authentication = "ActiveDirectoryPassword")

DBI::dbExecute(con, "COPY INTO <schema>.<table>
(<field_names>)
FROM 'https://<blob_storage_path>.gz'
WITH (
  FILE_TYPE = 'csv',
  CREDENTIAL = (IDENTITY = 'Storage Account Key',
SECRET = '<key_that_contains_alphanumeric_characters_plus_/_and_+_and_padding=='),

  COMPRESSION = 'gzip',
  FIELDQUOTE = ''  ,
  FIELDTERMINATOR = '\t',
  ROWTERMINATOR = '\n',
  FIRSTROW = 2
);")

```

title: Segfault appears on MS SQL SERVER queries on Skylake architecture since odbc 1.3.0
description:
### EDIT:

found the cause with R gdb the segfault appears in:
```
Thread 1 "R" received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.
0x00007ffff753e930 in __lll_unlock_elision () from /lib64/libpthread.so.0
```
googling the issue gave me [this explanation](https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/cf-process-crashes-segmentation-fault-when-hle-hardware-lock-elision-feature-enabled-os)

and [this fix](https://www.suse.com/support/kb/doc/?id=000019071) for my OS (OpenSuse) which was to disable hardware lock ellision...

Any input @jimhester  on how to go forward (disable what uses hle at the package level or at the user OS level?)

### tldr:
SQL SERVER queries segfault inside Gitlab CI (which runs on Intel Skylake) with latest odbc 1.3.0 and work fine in any other configuration (old version of odbc  or local docker image with new version of odbc but no Skylake)

I think I isolated the problem to a minimal example failing on SKylake architecture

```
> query = "SELECT name, time_utc FROM daylight_saving_time"
> 
> conn <- odbc::dbConnect(odbc::odbc(),
+ driver = "/usr/lib64/libtdsodbc.so",
+ server = "test.sql***",
+ database = "***",
+ uid = "***",
+ pwd = "***",
+ port = "***")
> 
> rs <- odbc::dbSendQuery(conn, query)
> res <- odbc::dbFetch(rs)
> res
                            name            time_utc
1    fall_change_backward_na_bst 2018-10-28 01:30:00
2  fall_change_backward_na_bstp1 2018-10-28 02:30:00
3   spring_change_forward_na_bst 2018-03-25 01:30:00
4 spring_change_forward_na_bstp1 2018-03-25 02:30:00
5                         summer 2018-07-01 22:00:00
6                         winter 2018-01-01 22:00:00
> odbc::dbClearResult(rs)

 *** caught segfault ***
address (nil), cause 'unknown'

Traceback:
 1: result_release(res@ptr)
 2: odbc::dbClearResult(rs)
 3: odbc::dbClearResult(rs)
An irrecoverable exception occurred. R is aborting now ...
```


So the problem lies in dbClearResult where it looks it has already been cleared?
Also I don't understand why the traceback indicates two calls to odbc::dbClearResult ?

### Issue Description and Expected Result

### Database
On MYSQL database it never fails
On SQL SERVER database it fails only on Skylake architecture

entry in .odbc.ini file is like this:

```
[MSSQLTEST]
Driver = /usr/lib64/libtdsodbc.so
Description = Connection to SQL server test
Trace           = Yes
TraceFile       = /tmp/odbctest.trace
Server = test.sql.***
Database = ***
Port = ***
User = ***
Password = ***

```

I can't reproduce the problem without the same context...


title: POSIXct losing precision on insert - Oracle
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
This is the same issue as #208 but for Oracle.  Milliseconds are lost when inserted.  The same code works with the ROracle package.

### Database
Oracle Database 19c Enterprise Edition

### Reproducible Example
```
options(digits.secs = 6)

df <- data.frame(DATETIME = Sys.time(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

library(odbc)

# the time has milliseconds in R
print(df)
#                     DATETIME
# 1 2020-09-19 22:51:55.485072

# odbc connection
con <- DBI::dbConnect(odbc::odbc(),
                      driver = "Oracle18",
                      uid = "username",
                      pwd = "password",
                      dbq = "database",
                      timezone = Sys.timezone(),
                      timezone_out = Sys.timezone())

DBI::dbExecute(con, "create table test_table (datetime timestamp(6))")

# insert data
DBI::dbExecute(con, "insert into test_table (datetime) values (:1)", params = df)

# the time does not have milliseconds when read back from Oracle
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "select * from test_table")
#              DATETIME
# 1 2020-09-19 22:58:03

DBI::dbExecute(con, "drop table test_table")


library(ROracle)

Sys.setenv(TZ = "EST5EDT",
           ORA_SDTZ = "EST5EDT")

# ROracle connection
con <- ROracle::dbConnect(ROracle::Oracle(),
                          username = "username",
                          password = "password",
                          dbname = "database")

DBI::dbExecute(con, "create table test_table (datetime timestamp(6))")

# insert data
DBI::dbExecute(con, "insert into test_table (datetime) values (:1)", data = df)
DBI::dbCommit(con)

# the time does have milliseconds when read back from Oracle
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "select * from test_table")
#                     DATETIME
# 1 2020-09-19 22:58:03.187895

DBI::dbExecute(con, "drop table test_table")
```

title: Use nanodbc::describe_parameters()
description:
instead of relying on `SQLDescribeParams()`. This feels like the more robust way -- to adapt parameter types to what the client sends rather than to what the server thinks it needs to receive.

Will require upgrading nanodbc. Upstream: https://github.com/nanodbc/nanodbc/pull/225. @jimhester: I can take a closer look if you think this is a good idea.

Related: #30.

I'm not sure if this is an issue with the Simba driver. The Microsoft driver (which is near unusable due to the "Invalid Descriptor Index" problem, #309) has this problem for local temporary tables. I have confirmed with printf debugging that this is caused by a failing `SQLDescribeParams()` call.

``` r
library(odbc)

db <- dbConnect(
  odbc(),
  dsn = "mssql-test-ms",
  uid = "kirill",
  pwd = keyring::key_get("mssql", "kirill")
)

sf <- data.frame(a = "1")
sf$SHAPE <- list(raw(10))

# Works with Microsoft drivers, doesn't work with FreeTDS
dbWriteTable(db, "##test", as.data.frame(sf))

# Doesn't work with either Microsoft or FreeTDS driver
dbWriteTable(db, "#test", as.data.frame(sf))
#> Error in result_insert_dataframe(rs@ptr, values, batch_rows): nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:1617: 00000: [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server][SQL Server]Implicit conversion from data type varchar to varbinary is not allowed. Use the CONVERT function to run this query.  [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server][SQL Server]Statement(s) could not be prepared.

# Works with Microsoft drivers, doesn't work with FreeTDS
dbWriteTable(db, "test", as.data.frame(sf))

dbRemoveTable(db, "test")
```

CC @mloskot @detule.

title: install odbc on PowerPC64 fails due to error in time_zone_libc.cc
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
We are trying to install `odbc` on a ppc64le/debian docker-container running on an IBM PowerPC 8.
While installing via `install.packages("odbc")` we get this error message:

```
g++ -std=gnu++11  -Wall -Iinclude -std=c++11 -pthread  -O -fPIC -MMD  -c -o time_zone_libc.o src/time_zone_libc.cc
src/time_zone_libc.cc: In member function ‘virtual cctz::Breakdown cctz::TimeZoneLibC::BreakTime(cctz::time_point<std::chrono:
src/time_zone_libc.cc:28:28: error: ‘struct tm’ has no member named ‘__tm_gmtoff’; did you mean ‘tm_gmtoff’?
 #  define OFFSET(tm) ((tm).__tm_gmtoff)
                            ^~~~~~~~~~~
src/time_zone_libc.cc:66:17: note: in expansion of macro ‘OFFSET’
     bd.offset = OFFSET(tm);
                 ^~~~~~
src/time_zone_libc.cc:29:28: error: ‘struct tm’ has no member named ‘__tm_zone’; did you mean ‘tm_zone’?
 #  define ABBR(tm)   ((tm).__tm_zone)
                            ^~~~~~~~~
src/time_zone_libc.cc:67:15: note: in expansion of macro ‘ABBR’
     bd.abbr = ABBR(tm);
               ^~~~
make[1]: *** [<builtin>: time_zone_libc.o] Error 1
make[1]: Leaving directory '/tmp/RtmpW6XDbP/R.INSTALL64de1ba355e5/odbc/src/cctz'
make: *** [Makevars:16: cctz/libcctz.a] Error 2
ERROR: compilation failed for package ‘odbc’
```

So we had a deeper look at the odbc/src/cctz/src/time_zone_libc.cc file:

```c++
// Define OFFSET(tm) and ABBR(tm) for your platform to return the UTC
// offset and zone abbreviation after a call to localtime_r().
#if defined(linux)
# if defined(__USE_BSD)
#  define OFFSET(tm) ((tm).tm_gmtoff)
#  define ABBR(tm)   ((tm).tm_zone)
# else
#  define OFFSET(tm) ((tm).__tm_gmtoff)
#  define ABBR(tm)   ((tm).__tm_zone)
# endif
```
Then we changed it to:
```c++
// Define OFFSET(tm) and ABBR(tm) for your platform to return the UTC
// offset and zone abbreviation after a call to localtime_r().
#if defined(linux)
# if defined(__USE_MISC)
#  define OFFSET(tm) ((tm).tm_gmtoff)
#  define ABBR(tm)   ((tm).tm_zone)
# else
#  define OFFSET(tm) ((tm).__tm_gmtoff)
#  define ABBR(tm)   ((tm).__tm_zone)
# endif
```
and installed the package successfully with this change.
 
Is there a way to add a `__USE_MISC` case in order to better integrate the odbc package with ppc64?

title: Asynchronous operation
description:
It would be great to be able to interrupt a query that takes a long time to run and return records. For this it seems we need to look into asynchronous execution with polling: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/odbc/reference/develop-app/asynchronous-execution-polling-method?redirectedfrom=MSDN&view=sql-server-ver15 .

A first glance into nanodbc suggests that some form of callback is supported. For drivers that support this, we could then execute asynchronously and poll for completion and also call `checkUserInterrupt()`.

title: Can't connect to Teradata using DBI + odbc unless I establish an RODBC connection first
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
Occasionally connecting to my Teradata database fails:
```r
# Fails
ch <- DBI::dbConnect(
      odbc::odbc(),
      Driver = "Teradata",
      DBCName = "my_database",
      AUTHENTICATION = "ldap",
      UID = "johndoe",
      PWD = "1234"
    )
# Error: nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:950: HYT00: [WSock32 DLL] 10060 WSA E TimedOut: No response received when attempting to connect to the Teradata server
```

However, if I first establish a connection using RODBC, which I know is an entirely different package, and then retry the connection, it works! It is so weird, but it's the only way I've found to make DBI + odbc connect again (except trying later):
```r
# Connect using RODBC
ch <- RODBC::odbcDriverConnect(sprintf("Driver={Teradata};DBCName=WMG;AUTHENTICATION=ldap;AUTHENTICATIONPARAMETER=%s@@%s", "johndoe", "1234"))

# Now it works
ch <- DBI::dbConnect(
      odbc::odbc(),
      Driver = "Teradata",
      DBCName = "my_database",
      AUTHENTICATION = "ldap",
      UID = "johndoe",
      PWD = "1234"
```

title: Cannot read unicode from "PostgreSQL Unicode(x64)"
description:
**Steps to reproduce:**
* Connect to some postgre database in windows using connection string with driver `PostgreSQL Unicode(x64)`. Optionally, specify the encoding to be UTF-8 in the `dbConnect` argument. Example:
```r
con <- DBI::dbConnect(odbc::odbc(),
    .connection_string = "Driver={PostgreSQL Unicode(x64)`};Server=server;Port=5432;Database=db;
Uid=user;Pwd=pwd;",
    encoding = "UTF-8")
```
* Retrieve data from some table (not from some self-sufficient statement like `select 'str'`) through `dbGetQuery` (from any package, e.g. `DBI`, `RPostgreSQL`, `RPostgres`). Example:
```r
df <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "select problem_col from some_table limit 10")
```
* Inspect said data in R.

**Expected results:** output `data.frame` from `dbGetQuery` should have the data as it is in the table, encoded in UTF-8.

**Actual results:** all the non-ascii characters get replaced with question marks, and the encoding from R's `Encoding(char_vector)` is `"unknown"`. Forcing it to some other encoding does not make a difference.

The problem is not present in linux with driver `PostgreSQL UNICODE` (which is not accepted under windows).

title: MS Access encoding error: result_fetch() failed with Incomplete multibyte sequence

<!--Example: `dbGetQuery()` returns incorrect timestamps.-->
`dbGetQuery()` gets "Error in result_fetch(res@ptr, n, ...) : Incomplete multibyte sequence" when accessing a MS Access database with GBK/CP936 (Chinese) encoding.

> It looks quite normal in Access and I can successfully read it into R using `RODBC::sqlQuery()`. But when I run the following codes, it failed with warning "Error in result_fetch(res@ptr, n, ...) : Incomplete multibyte sequence".

### Database
<!--Example: PostgreSQL 9.5, SQL Server 2012-->
MS Access 2016 (64-bit)

```r
[1] "ACEODBC.DLL"

[1] "03.80.0000"

$driver.version
[1] "Microsoft Access database engine"

$odbcdriver.version
[1] "03.51"

$supports.transactions
[1] FALSE
```

### Reproducible Example
<!--
If possible include a _small_ dump of the table with the error and the R code
that generates the error. In your reprex please use `con` as the name of the
connection, this makes it easier to run locally.

The reprex package can be helpful in doing this.

    install.packages("reprex")
    reprex::reprex()

Example:
```r
library(odbc)
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(odbc::odbc(), dsn = "PostgreSQL")
dbWriteTable(con, "iris", iris)
dbReadTable(con, "iris")
```
-->
__Testcase__: [test.zip](https://github.com/tidyverse/dplyr/files/2991236/test.zip)

By the following codes, you will get the multibyte incomplete error.

```r
library(dplyr)
con <- DBI::dbConnect(
    odbc::odbc(), 
    .connection_string=paste0("Driver={Microsoft Access Driver (*.mdb, *.accdb)};
                               Dbq=<testcase .accdb file>"), 
    encoding="CP936")
tbl(con, "Table1") %>% select(Place) %>% collect 
```

If you change `encoding="CP936"` to `"UTF-8"`,

```r
con <- DBI::dbConnect(
    odbc::odbc(), 
    .connection_string=paste0("Driver={Microsoft Access Driver (*.mdb, *.accdb)};
                               Dbq=<a .accdb file>"), 
    encoding="UTF-8")
tbl(con, "Table1") %>% select(Place) %>% collect 
```
you will get the following

```
# A tibble: 3 x 1
  Place                                                      
  <chr>                                                      
1 "\xd5\xe3\xbd\xad-\xba\xbc\xd6\xdd-\xce\xf7\xcf\xaa"       
2 "\xb1\xb1\xbe\xa9-\xb9\xfa\xbc\xd2\xb9\xe3\xb8\xe6\xb2\xfa"
3 "\xd5\xe3\xbd\xad-\xba\xbc\xd6\xdd-\xce\xf7\xcf\xaa\xfa" 
```

Row 1 and 3 should have been identical, but in fact row 3 has 15 bytes, which I guess triggered the error.

Additions:

- By `dbGetQuery(con, "select * from Table1")`, you can get the identical results.
- The issue was previously submitted to [tidyverse/dbplyr issue#270](https://github.com/tidyverse/dbplyr/issues/270), but they advise that this is likely to be caused by `odbc` package.

title: Unable to list columns in Hive
description:
We’re having a hard time reading the catalog for our Hive instance. It’s possible that the Hive metadata are messed up, but the fact I can query data would suggest otherwise. The problem is that the odbcListColumns is not picking up the table info (and the connections pane also shows no table details). This is easy to reproduce on desktop pro. Would you mind taking a look?

```
con <- dbConnect(odbc::odbc(),
                 Driver = "hive",
                 Host = "***",
                 Port = 32796,
                 UID = "***",
                 PWD = "***"
)
odbc::odbcListColumns(con, table = "test_table", schema = "default") # empty
DBI::dbReadTable(con, "test_table") # succeeds
```

`odbcListObjects` returns the correct schema, so that function is working. But `odbcListColumns` returns nothing. It is possible that the Hive metadata are messed up (wouldn’t be the first time).

title: Cassandra throws error due to missing primary key
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
Cassandra requires that all tables have a primary key (see [docs](http://cassandra.apache.org/doc/latest/cql/ddl.html?)). When `DataTypes.R` is updated for Cassandra with the following:
```r
`odbcDataType.Cassandra` <- function(con, obj, ...) {
  switch_type(obj,
    factor = "TEXT",
    datetime = "TIMESTAMP",
    time = "TIME",
    date = "DATE",
    binary = "BLOB",
    integer = "BIGINT",
    double = "DOUBLE",
    character = "TEXT",
    logical = "BOOLEAN",
    stop("Unsupported type", call. = FALSE)
  )
}
```

```
Error: <SQL> 'CREATE TABLE "cars" ( "row_names" TEXT, "mpg" DOUBLE, "cyl" DOUBLE, "disp" DOUBLE, "hp" DOUBLE, "drat" DOUBLE, "wt" DOUBLE, "qsec" DOUBLE, "vs" DOUBLE, "am" DOUBLE, "gear" DOUBLE, "carb" DOUBLE ) ' nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:1587: HY000: [RStudio][CassandraODBC] (120) Primary key need to be defined for CREATE TABLE statement.
```

title: copy_to not working with given types since odbc 1.3.0
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
copy_to not working with given types since odbc 1.3.0

### Database
SQL Server 2016

### Reproducible Example
Example:
```r
library(dplyr)
library(DBI)

con <- dbConnect(odbc::odbc(), .connection_string = "Driver={ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server};Server= ;Database= ;Uid= ;\nPwd= ;\n",  timeout = 100)

dat <- data.frame(x = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), 3), y = rep(c(1, 2, 3), 3), z = rep(NA, 9), d = rep(as.Date("1999-09-09"), 9))

copy_to(con, dat, types = c(
  "varchar(1)",
  "numeric(3,1)",
  "date",
  "date"
), overwrite = TRUE
)

copy_to(con, dat, types = c(
  "varchar(1)",
  "numeric(3,1)",
  "date",
  "date"
),
temporary = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE
)
```

copy_to stops with the following error message. With odbc 1.2.3 everything is working fine, but since 1.3.0 the error occurs.

```r
Fehler in .local(conn, name, value, ...) : 
  rlang::is_null(field.types) || (rlang::is_named(field.types)) is not TRUE
```

title: Help installing with clang on RHEL7
description:
I'd really like to install (from source) the latest version of `odbc`, but at work we're on RedHat 7 so our version of `gcc` is rather old (4.8.5) and predates full C++11 support. This has been well documented, for eaxmple [here](https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/360052331933-ODBC-v1-2-3-on-CentOS-RHEL-6-7-). Unfortunately, our Linux admins are strongly discouraging us from using RedHat Software Collections, so the solution in that article doesn't work for us.

While they discourage the use of RedHat Software Collections, our Linux admins are fine with us `yum install`'ing packages from EPEL. I noticed that `clang v3.4.2` is available for RHEL7 from EPEL, and according to [clang.llvm.org/cxx_status](https://clang.llvm.org/cxx_status), "Clang 3.3 and later implement all of the ISO C++ 2011 standard." So I `yum install`'ed `clang` and added `CXX11 = clang++` to my `~/.R/Makevars` file. 
  
After doing this, I got an error about `'codecvt' file not found`. Some Googling led me to understand that this is a C++11 header missing from `gcc`'s standard library, so I `yum install`'ed `libcxx-devel` (also available in EPEL) and added `CXX11FLAGS += -stdlib=libc++` to my `~/.R/Makevars` file. Now everything seems to compile just fine, but `install.packages` throws the following error upon trying to load the package:

```
Error: unable to load shared object '/mnt/r/site-library/4.0/00LOCK-odbc/00new/odbc/libs/odbc.so':
  /mnt/r/site-library/4.0/00LOCK-odbc/00new/odbc/libs/odbc.so: undefined symbol: _ZTINSt3_113basic_ostreamIcNS_11char_traitsIcEEEE
```

I don't really know my way around C++ compilation, so could someone please point me in the right direction to getting this to compile with `clang`?

**Recap:**
* Using R 4.0.2 on RHEL7
* `yum install clang clang-devel libcxx libcxx-devel` to get a C++11 compliant compiler
* `~/.R/Makevars` contains:
```
CXX11 = clang++
CXX11FLAGS += -stdlib=libc++
```
* Error message:
```
Error: unable to load shared object '/mnt/r/site-library/4.0/00LOCK-odbc/00new/odbc/libs/odbc.so':
  /mnt/r/site-library/4.0/00LOCK-odbc/00new/odbc/libs/odbc.so: undefined symbol: _ZTINSt3_113basic_ostreamIcNS_11char_traitsIcEEEE
```

title: Custom sqlCreateTable methods that take additional arguments?
description:
I notice that in `R/db.R`, there are "custom" `sqlCreateTable` methods defined for RDBMSs that don't use the typical `CREATE TABLE` syntax (I think all of these so far are for non-standard syntax when creating a temporary table). I notice that in every case, the method definition takes additional arguments via `...`, but doesn't do anything with them. What do you think about  allowing users to modify the `CREATE TABLE` statement via arguments passed to `...`? Here's an example that allows users to specify the [storage format](https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/Hive/LanguageManual+DDL#LanguageManualDDL-StorageFormatsStorageFormatsRowFormat,StorageFormat,andSerDe) of a Hive table by adding e.g. `stored_as = "ORC"` to their `dbWriteTable` call:

```R
setMethod("sqlCreateTable", "Hive",
  function(con, table, fields, field.types = NULL, row.names = NA, temporary = FALSE, ...) {
    table <- dbQuoteIdentifier(con, table)
    fields <- createFields(con, fields, field.types, row.names)
    the_dots <- list(...)

    SQL(paste0(
        "CREATE ", if (temporary) " TEMPORARY ", "TABLE ", table, " (\n",
        "  ", paste(fields, collapse = ",\n  "), "\n)\n",
        if ("stored_as" %in% names(the_dots)) paste("STORED AS", the_dots$stored_as)
    ))
  })
```

Does this make sense to implement this way? At what point do we just say that the user needs to write their own `CREATE TABLE` statement and run it with `dbExecute`? How would we document these optional arguments?

Let me know what you think about this - I have a few of these I'd be interested in implementing (table compression for DB2, using the `NOT LOGGED` option when creating a temporary table in DB2, `STORED AS` for Hive, `PARTITIONED BY` for Hive, etc, etc). But I don't want to spam you with these if you think this isn't helpful.

title: dbGetQuery results in Error in new_result(connection@ptr, statement, immediate) :    std::bad_alloc error
description:
I get a bad_alloc error when trying to connect to a DB2 database (called ODS below) via 64bit DB2 drivers via 64bit R/Rstudio installed in Linux (Ubuntu 18.04)

```R
## Code
library(odbc)
con <- dbConnect(odbc::odbc(), "ODS", uid = "sample_user",pwd="password",timeout = 10)
--connects successfully

a <- dbGetQuery(con,'SELECT * FROM SAMPLE_DATABASE')
--Error in new_result(connection@ptr, statement, immediate) : 
--std::bad_alloc
``` 

On searching, RODBC driver also results in a similar error:

```R
library(RODBC)
myconn <-odbcConnect("ODS", uid="sample_user", pwd="password")
sqlQuery(myconn, "SELECT * FROM SAMPLE_DATABASE")
--Error in odbcFetchRows(channel, max = max, buffsize = buffsize, nullstring = nullstring,  : 
 --negative length vectors are not allowed
```

which is resolved by adding the believeNRows=FALSE option as below:

```R
myconn <-odbcConnect("ODS", uid="sample_user", pwd="password", believeNRows=FALSE)
sqlQuery(myconn, "SELECT * FROM SAMPLE_DATABASE")
--Works successfully
```

As per a stackoverflow post, this is caused by SQLRowCount to be 4294967295 (even if there's just one row) on 64bit Linux while it reports -1 on 32 bit Linux. This is circumvented in RODBC by the believeNRows=FALSE option.

Is the odbc running into the issue because of some different behaviour between 32bit and 64bit? Is there any way to resolve this for the odbc library as well?

I have confirmed via db2cli tool that sql output of the above query in command-line via the DB2 driver works perfectly.

title: clarify 'immediate=' verbiage
description:
*Hey everybody, long time no chat! Is anyone going to an in-person R or INFORMS conference any time soon? I think I owe many of you a beer or something :-)*

(This might be somewhat of a dupe of #127, but I think I'm geared more towards documentation here.)

### Issue Description and Expected Result

The verbiage for `immediate=` suggests that the driver auto-reattempts with the other API if the first attempt fails. I'm having a hard time understanding when to specific `immediate=`, and consequences of using it incorrectly.

Namely, using a simple query on a local table,

```r
qry <- "select top 1 * from tablename t where t.Id=?"
prms <- list("203A8526-2992-EB11-A2DD-D094661AB20C")
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, qry, params=prms)
## WORKS
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, qry, params=prms, immediate=FALSE)
## WORKS

# Error in new_result(connection@ptr, statement, immediate) : 
#   nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:1594: 07002: [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server]COUNT field incorrect or syntax error 
```

Okay, now a slightly different query:

```r
qry <- "select top 1 * into #sometemp from tablename"

DBI::dbExecute(con, qry)
# [1] 1
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "select * from #sometemp")
# Error: nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:1655: 42000: [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server][SQL Server]Invalid object name '#sometemp'.  [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server][SQL Server]Statement(s) could not be prepared.
```

From the verbiage in the `?DBI::dbGetQuery` section on "Specification for the 'immediate' argument", I would have thought that I could trust that the backend would handle this automatically for me.

title: Feature request: dbWriteTable with different column names in data.frame and DB table
description:
A stackoverflow user asked how to do this and there is only a work-around so far, see:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/64950837/cant-insert-dataframe-to-sqlite-table-when-column-names-different-dbwritetable

I suggest to support different column names as long as the number, type and order of columns are the same between the `data.frame` and the DB table. In other words: Use the column position instead of the name...

Renaming the names of the `data.frame` itself would be possible of course but has possible side-effects
(eg. if you do not want to change the column names just to upload the data into a DB table but reuse the original names in downstream R code).

title: Wrong data type for datetime for Spark
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
If I try to insert data containing datetimes into a Spark server, it creates a DATE field and then tries to insert the datetime values into that, causing a `Error: nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:1752: 22008: [Simba][Support] (40520) Datetime field overflow resulting from invalid datetime` error. 

If would expect a `TIMESTAMP` field to be created for datetime values.

### Database
Tested on DataBricks Spark

### Reproducible Example
```r
db <- DBI::dbConnect(odbc::odbc(),
                     Driver = "Simba Spark ODBC Driver",
                     Host = keyring::key_get("dataBricksServer"),
                     uid = keyring::key_get("dataBricksUser"),
                     pwd = keyring::key_get("dataBricksPassword"),
                     HTTPPath = keyring::key_get("dataBricksHttpPath"),
                     SSL = 1,
                     ThriftTransport = 2,
                     AuthMech = 3,
                     Port = keyring::key_get("dataBricksPort"))
DBI::dbWriteTable(
  conn = db,
  name =  DBI::Id(schema = "scratch", table = "insert_test"),
  value = data.frame(dt = Sys.time()),
  overwrite = TRUE,
  append = FALSE
)
# Error: nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:1752: 22008: [Simba][Support] (40520) Datetime field overflow resulting from invalid datetime
```

If I change [this line](https://github.com/r-dbi/odbc/blob/main/R/DataTypes.R#L95) to read `datetime = "TIMESTAMP",`, all is well. I'll create a PR in case you want to use it.

title: Can't open lib '/opt/homebrew/lib/libmsodbcsql.18.dylib' : file not found
description:
Hi,

I'm trying to connect to a SQL Server database through R using `{odbc}`. Like many others, I'm struggling.

I started by installing the latest version of the Microsoft ODBC driver [here](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/connect/odbc/linux-mac/install-microsoft-odbc-driver-sql-server-macos?view=sql-server-ver15) and followed the troubleshooting to ensure that the appropriate files are symlinked.

I have an M1 MacBook Pro and have got to the point where I can run the appropriate `isql` command in the terminal and return a database connection, but trying the following:

`
con <-  DBI::dbConnect(odbc::odbc(),
                       Driver = "ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server",
                       server = "server_name",
                       Database = "db",
                       UID = "",
                       PWD = "",
                       port = 1433)
`

Where `ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server` is pointing to `odbcinst.ini` file which contains:

`[ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server]
Description=Microsoft ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server
Driver=/opt/homebrew/lib/libmsodbcsql.18.dylib
UsageCount=2`

Results in:

`Error: nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:1021: 00000: [unixODBC][Driver Manager]Can't open lib '/opt/homebrew/lib/libmsodbcsql.18.dylib' : file not found`

The issue seems to be that my R instance can't locate the `libmsodbcsql.18.dylib` file.

Any help would be much appreciated. I've already considered the following links:

- https://github.com/microsoft/homebrew-mssql-release/issues/53
- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/61628762/cant-open-lib-odbc-driver-17-for-sql-server-in-python

title: Connection dropping prefix of the tables
dbGetQuery no longer works with stored procedures
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
I've just install R version 4.0.3 (until last week I was using R 3.6) with DBI 1.1.1 and I'm facing a new error that I've never seen before. I have a MySQL database (version 8.0.18) and I use DBI to retrieve data. Specifically, the database includes some stored procedures that prepare a sql statement based on input parameters and execute it. Until last week I was able to retrieve the output of these stored procedures using dbGetQuery (as indicated in the DBI documentation) while after the upgrade to R 4.0.3
I get the following error:
 
Error in result_fetch(res@ptr, n) : 
  nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:2695: 24000: [MySQL][ODBC 8.0(w) Driver][mysqld-8.0.23]Fetch without a SELECT 

### Database
[MySQL][ODBC 8.0(w) Driver][mysqld-8.0.23]

### Reproducible Example
Assume there is a simple table called "test_1" like this:
intId          |          strName
1               |          Rome
2               |          New York
3               |          Prague
and a stored procedure # called "my_stored_proc" with two input parameters (table_name and id) and the following structure:

BEGIN:
	SET @t1 =CONCAT('SELECT strName FROM ', table_name, ' WHERE intId =', id, ';' );
	PREPARE stmt3 FROM @t1;
	EXECUTE stmt3;
	DEALLOCATE PREPARE stmt3;
END

In R I then run the following code:

```r

library(odbc)
library(DBI)
strCnn <- paste0("Driver={MySQL ODBC 8.0 UNICODE Driver};
                              Server=***;
                              Database=***;
                              Port=***;
                              User=***;
                              Password=***;
                              trusted_connection=true;
                              ENABLE_LOCAL_INFILE=1;")
cnn <- dbConnect(odbc::odbc(), .connection_string = strCnn, bigint="numeric"

ref_tbl <- "test_1"
ref_id <- 1
out <- paste0("CALL my_stored_proc('", ref_tbl, "', ", ref_id, ");") %>% dbGetQuery(CNN_NOAH, .) %>% as.numeric()

```

In the paste the above code returns out == "Rome" while I now get the error mentioned above.

Is this an error on my side or a bug?

Thank you in advance
Isacco
